exam_scheme.note: The Joint Entrance Examination (Advanced) is conducted by the seven zonal Indian Institutes of Technology (IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Guwahati, IIT Kanpur, IIT Kharagpur, IIT Madras, and IIT Roorkee) under the guidance of the Joint Admission Board (JAB). Only the top ~2,50,000 candidates qualifying JEE (Main) across categories are eligible to appear. The examination comprises two mandatory papers—Paper 1 and Paper 2—both held on the same day in Computer Based Test (CBT) mode (3 hours each). Both papers test Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics with varying question types (single choice, multi-correct with partial marking, numerical value, and matching lists). Candidates must appear in both papers to be eligible for ranking and admission to undergraduate engineering and science programmes across 23 IITs through JoSAA.
